title: Generation of E. coli MG1655 Whole Cell Lysate for Proteomics Applications
author: David Butcher
materials: Chill lysates on ice for 5 mins.

steps.title: Streak E. coli on agar plates
steps.instruction: Streak E. coli samples on non‑selective LB and/or M9 minimal agar plates. Incubate at 37 °C until colonies are visible and well separated (12–16 h for LB, 16–24 h for M9). To avoid overgrowth, incubate 4–5 h at 37 °C then finish at room temperature overnight.

steps.title: Inoculate Bio‑Reaction tubes
steps.instruction: Inoculate each Bio‑Reaction tube with 50 µL (1/300th volume) of saturated overnight culture. For smaller cultures use 15 mL tubes with 5 mL medium and inoculate with 17 µL. Optionally weigh 50 mL tubes before adding media and record tare weight.

steps.title: Add liquid growth media
steps.instruction: Add 5 mL of sterile liquid media to sterilized 16 × 150 mm culture tubes (or to 15 mL Bio‑Reaction tubes). Prepare two tubes per growth condition/medium type. For larger scale, add 15 mL of sterile liquid media to 50 mL Bio‑Reaction tubes.

steps.title: Incubate cultures with shaking
steps.instruction: Place culture tubes in an orbital shaker at 250 rpm, 37 °C. Incubate overnight (~16 h) until the medium is cloudy and saturated with cells. Monitor OD₆₀₀ with a UV‑vis spectrophotometer and plot a growth curve; use an extra discard tube for OD measurements if needed.

steps.title: Harvest cells by centrifugation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge tubes at 4 000 × g (≈6 000 RPM on F15‑8x50cy rotor), 4 °C for 15 min. Decant supernatant (hazardous waste; autoclave or bleach). Keep the cell pellets.

steps.title: Freeze cell pellets
steps.instruction: Seal tube lids with Parafilm (or use lids without pores) and freeze pellets at –80 °C for at least 1 hour (or until ready for lysis).

steps.title: Prepare fresh lysis buffer
steps.instruction: Mix the following to make 10 mL lysis buffer (scale as needed): 0.2 mL 1 M Tris base, pH 7.5 (20 mM final); 0.2 mL 5 M NaCl (100 mM); 1 mL 10 % w/v N‑lauroylsarcosine (1 % w/v); 0.1 mL 100× HALT inhibitor cocktail (1×); 8.5 mL HPLC‑grade water. Chill on ice. Use an EDTA‑free inhibitor if a nuclease will be added; if EDTA is present, double the MgCl₂ added later.

steps.title: Thaw pellets and resuspend
steps.instruction: Thaw frozen pellets on ice for 15 min. Resuspend each pellet in chilled lysis buffer at a ratio of 1 mL buffer per 5 mL original culture volume.

steps.title: Add MgCl₂ to lysate
steps.instruction: Add 1 µL of 1 M MgCl₂ per 1 mL lysate to achieve a final Mg²⁺ concentration of 1 mM.

steps.title: Add nuclease for DNA digestion
steps.instruction: Add nuclease to each mL of lysate: either 0.5 µL (125 U) Benzonase HC or 10 µL (20 U) NEB DNase I. Pipette to mix thoroughly. Skip this step if a subsequent sonication will be used; increase sonication cycles if needed.

steps.title: Optional sonication of lysate
steps.instruction: Place the tube with resuspended pellet on ice. Set the sonicator to the lowest power, position the probe tip near the bottom without touching. Pulse for 5 cycles of 10 s on, 30 s off, adjusting power until the buffer surface agitates without foaming.

steps.title: Incubate lysate on ice
steps.instruction: Incubate the lysate on ice for 20 min, swirling gently every 5 min.

steps.title: Centrifuge to remove debris
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the lysate at 12 500 × g (≈10 400 RPM on F15‑8x50cy rotor) for 20 min at 4 °C. Collect the supernatant and discard the pellet.

steps.title: Incubate lysate at 37 °C
steps.instruction: Incubate the cleared lysate at 37 °C for 20 min, inverting the tube every 5 min to mix.

steps.title: Determine protein concentration
steps.instruction: Measure total protein concentration of each lysate using a BCA assay or another appropriate method.

steps.title: Aliquot and store lysates
steps.instruction: Aliquot lysate into portions suitable for downstream applications (e.g., 50 µg or 100 µg for proteomics). Store aliquots at –80 °C; thaw each aliquot only once to minimize protein degradation.
